draft.title: Short-term and long-term causes
card: a condition that builds up over years or decades and makes an event more likely. It sets the scene but does not make the event happen on its own.
a more recent event that sparks the outcome, often called a trigger. It has its effect because the long-term causes are already in place.
what follows from an event. Some are intended, which means the people involved wanted them. Others are unintended, which means nobody planned them.
Example: the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in June 1914 was a trigger for the First World War. Tensions between the great powers had built up for many years before it.
draft.remember: Long-term causes build the pressure. Triggers set the event off. Consequences can be planned or not.

a.q: Which statement best describes a trigger of a historical event?
opts: A recent event that sparks an outcome already made likely
A slow change that builds up over many decades
A result of the event that nobody planned
A reason the event was intended by its leaders
a.why: A trigger is a short-term cause that sparks an event when long-term conditions are already in place. A slow build-up over decades describes a long-term cause, which is the most tempting wrong option.
a.clue: Think about what sets an event off, not what prepares for it.

b.q: For years, a town in Victoria suffered falling crop prices and rising debts. Then a bank suddenly called in its loans and farmers marched in protest. Which is the best description of the bank's decision?
opts: A short-term cause, which sparked the protest
A long-term cause, which built up over years
An unintended consequence of the protest
An intended consequence of the protest
b.why: The bank's decision was recent and sudden, and it sparked the protest because the long-term problems were already there. The falling prices and debts are the long-term causes. The decision came before the protest, so it cannot be a consequence of it.
b.clue: Ask whether the decision came before or after the protest, and whether it built up slowly or happened suddenly.

a.best: A recent event that sparks an outcome already made likely

b.best: A short-term cause, which sparked the protest
